stages.name: sense
stages.mechanism: webhooks, CI evidence ingestion, maintenance signals, audit events

stages.name: plan
stages.mechanism: architect-issued Work Orders (Issues → spec/work-orders/), governed Work Item creation

stages.name: check
stages.mechanism: revision-bound assertion evaluation at lifecycle gates, adaptive assurance depth

stages.name: execute
stages.mechanism: the execution fabric: eligibility, routing, agent runs

engineeringControlLoop.rule: The loop is composed ENTIRELY of existing authorities. No stage introduces a second engine; the control plane is connective tissue (repository-resident state + deterministic queries).

selection.rule: first-match over the declared change-surface flags; unclassified/unknown surfaces fail closed to the HIGH_ASSURANCE floor
selection.determinism: the same declared surfaces always select the same profile (pure function, no environment inputs)

assuranceProfiles.dominanceRule: Each profile's required checkpoint kinds must be a superset of the kinds the WORK-051 IMPACT_CHECKPOINT_MATRIX applies at every impact level the profile covers; a profile adds assurance depth, never subtracts (ADR-0002).
assuranceProfiles.authorityRule: Profiles change REQUIRED ASSURANCE DEPTH ONLY (which checkpoint contracts apply, which proof classes are required, what evidence must be recorded). They never change authority semantics: the same /work-items, /workflows, /agents, /verification, /reviews, /architecture and provider authorities remain authoritative in every profile.

checkpointContracts.statement: Durable identities with idempotent replay at every external boundary: same logical key ⇒ same durable outcome; no duplicate authorities created by retries.

BLOCKER 4 — two CONCURRENT same-key evaluations converge on EXACTLY ONE run + ONE evidence set

checkpointContracts.statement: Concurrent governed operations serialize or converge (database-level fencing, unique identities, create-or-converge); a crash leaves no partial durable state; recovery converges without duplication.

enforcement.marker: WORK-051 round 4 — ONE durable identity boundary for create AND adopt (the PR #52 review, BLOCKER 2 + BLOCKER 3)

checkpointContracts.statement: External effects (PR creation, provider calls) happen only through owned ports behind governed gates, with durable intent first and idempotent create-or-converge semantics; no pre-gate capability exists.

enforcement.marker: WORK-051 invariants — Architecture Governance and Checkpoints

checkpointContracts.statement: Checkpoint evidence is bound to the exact implementation revision (provider-observed snapshot identity); no working-tree fallback; mutated trees under the same revision label are detectable.

PROOF 4 — two GENUINELY DIFFERENT revisions produce distinct results, and mutating the on-disk fixture does NOT change a bound revision result (BLOCKER 1)
PROOF 11 — WorkflowOS evaluates ITSELF through the revision-bound snapshot: real detectors over the real backend tree, claim-authority evidence
PR #52 round 2 (HIGH 1) — the provider-observed snapshot identity DIFFERS when the same revision label serves different bytes (a mutated tree is detectable in the evidence)

may: plan its own implementation (architect-issued Work Orders, the planner, the dependency DAG)
execute changes to its own implementation through the execution fabric
verify its own changes (evidence-bound verification, CI ingestion)
review its own changes through /reviews (the architect's semantic authority)
maintain itself (maintenance signals feeding governed Work Items)
evaluate its own architecture conformance at any exact revision through the checkpoint substrate
mayNot: silently rewrite its frozen governing architecture — changes require the architecture-change/versioning authority (Work Order + new immutable version)
silently rewrite its own architecture authority or foundational rules
let a self-hosted worker merge its own governing PR — PR review by the architect is the only merge gate
introduce a second workflow engine or lifecycle authority
introduce a second Work Item authority
introduce a second verification or evidence authority
weaken tenant isolation or server-side security invariants
depend on chat/conversation state for governance
store governance state outside the repository (the repository is the durable source of truth for the self-hosting program)
coreProhibitions: silently rewrite its frozen governing architecture — changes require the architecture-change/versioning authority (Work Order + new immutable version)
introduce a second workflow engine or lifecycle authority

rules: one Work Item per implementation branch/PR
dependency eligibility: an item is eligible only when every declared dependency is complete
surface declarations + conflict detection: two in_flight work orders sharing a declared surface are a reported conflict (not parallel-safe without explicit architect coordination)
scope integrity: a worker edits only its own declared surfaces; cross-scope edits require a Work Order amendment
centralized architecture decisions: Work Orders + ADRs are the only decision entry points
PR review by the architect is the merge gate

coordination records are MUTUAL: a declared coordination between two in-flight work orders appears on BOTH records, covers every incomplete dependency the start was coordinated over, and one-sided declarations are invalid state

feedbackRule: Runtime/user/maintenance feedback enters governed planning ONLY through existing producers (WORK-040 planner, WORK-041 maintenance engine, verification failures, reviews) creating governed Work Items; the program state records each work order's origin so the loop's learn stage is durable. No new feedback engine exists.

detector.registry: the WORK-051 closed detector registry, advanced 6→7 by WORK-052 (docs/adr/ADR-0006-governance-manifest-detector.md)
detector.semantics: fail closed: missing/unreadable/invalid manifests are inconclusive; a weakened boundary, cyclic DAG, evidence-inconsistent status, unknown vocabulary, or missing enforcement references fail

completionRule.rule: status 'complete' ⇔ mergedAs merge evidence (pr + mergeCommit): the architect's merge of the implementation PR into main is the ONLY completion event.
completionRule.checkpointOutcomesAre: implementer-recorded, revision-bound CLAIMS that support the architect's PR review; they never transition status and never substitute the merge — a work order with every outcome evidenced but no merge is still in_flight.
completionRule.inFlightInvariant: an in_flight work order carries a branch and NO mergedAs evidence — merged-but-in-flight is a lie about the merge.
completionRule.historicalNote: WORK-001..WORK-051 completed before this rule was recorded; their merge evidence alone satisfies it (checkpoint outcomes were not part of their contracts).
